This is an essay written by an international student.

The Yamada Family and Me

Anna

Last week, I visited my friend Yamada’s house. Since Yamada’s house was far from my apartment, I had to take a train and a bus. It was my first time taking a train and a bus, so I was very anxious: “What should I do if I take the wrong train or bus?” When I told Yamada this, Yamada asked their father to drive to my apartment to pick me up. Yamada’s father immediately agreed: “Of course!”

When I arrived at Yamada’s house, Yamada’s mother and younger sister, who was in high school, came out to greet me. I gave the Yamada family a souvenir I had bought in my hometown and said, “Let’s drink it together!” At that moment, everyone looked slightly uncomfortable. The souvenir I had bought was wine. In my country, people drink wine while sharing a meal. However, Yamada’s parents could not drink alcohol, and Yamada and the younger sister were not yet allowed to drink. I thought, “I’ve ruined everything!” I thought that if I was going to buy a souvenir, （it would have been better to ask beforehand what the family liked）. However, the Yamada family said that they were happy because it was a rare wine, and they accepted it cheerfully.

After that, we all made and ate takoyaki, played games, and talked a lot. It was truly a very enjoyable day.

Regarding the Use of Aozora University Library

● Eligible users

Undergraduate students, international students, and faculty members of Aozora University

Undergraduate students, international students, and faculty members of Sakura University and Umino University located in Aozora City

● Hours of use

Monday ~ Friday: 8:30 ~ 20:00

Saturday: 9:00 ~ 17:00

● How to use the library

When undergraduate students, international students, and faculty members of Aozora University use the library, they should use the library card issued by the university.

When undergraduate students, international students, and faculty members of universities other than Aozora University use the library for the first time, they should obtain a library card at the reception desk.

● Borrowing

Present your library card together with the book or CD you wish to borrow at the reception desk.

Books may be borrowed for 2 weeks.

CDs and DVDs may be borrowed for 1 week.

● Returning items

Return books or CDs at the reception desk.

When the library is closed, place them in the book-return box in front of the entrance.

CDs and DVDs must not be placed in the book-return box; they must be returned at the reception desk.

● Notes

When photocopying a book, fill out a photocopying application form and submit it at the reception desk.

If you soil or lose a library book, be sure to contact the library.

Aozora University Library

default.p.goukakumoshi2_n4-t8-p1.vietnamese:
Summer in Japan

Amelia Taylor

Summer is my favorite season. Summer in Japan begins in June. June is called the 「rainy season (Tsuyu)」, and it rains all day long. However, vegetables and rice cannot grow without rain, so the 「rainy season」 is very important. The 「rainy season」 ends in July.

When July arrives, summer vacation begins, so children do not have to go to school. They play with their friends, go swimming, or do their homework.

August is the hottest month. From the 13th to the 15th is the 「Obon holiday」. During the 「Obon holiday」, many people travel or visit their grandparents, who live far away. Although summer in Japan is hot, there are many enjoyable things, such as the sea, swimming pools, fireworks festivals, and traditional festivals.

That is why I love summer so much.

✅ Correct answer: (c) 食べる前に料理の写真を撮ること
In the passage, 「そういうこと」 refers to taking photos of the food before eating, because this made the ramen become cold and less delicious.
default.q.goukakumoshi2_n4-t10-q1.explanation: 「そういうこと」 means “such an action,” with 「そういう」 referring to the content mentioned immediately before and 「こと」 turning an action into a noun. The sentence containing the answer means: “Because I think food should be eaten when it is at its most delicious, I want people not to do such things.” The supporting original sentence is: 「最近、ごはんを食べる前に写真を撮る人が増えてきました。私は、料理は一番おいしいときに食べるべきだと思うので、そういうことをしないでほしいと思います。」 Tip for distinguishing the closest option: (b) is the consequence that the food became cold, whereas (c) is the action replaced by 「そういうこと」.
default.q.goukakumoshi2_n4-t11-q1.verdict:
✅ Correct answer: (d) 3,100円
The 2,500円 shirt costs 200円 for shipping because it is below 3,000円; the expedited delivery service adds 300円, and the message card adds 100円. The total is 3,100円.
default.q.goukakumoshi2_n4-t11-q1.explanation: The pattern 「〜場合は、〜かかります」 means “if/in the case of doing ~, it costs ~,” and is used to state an additional charge. Because the buyer wants the item delivered earlier than the standard three-day delivery and wants to add a message card, both the 300円 expedited-delivery fee and the 100円 card fee apply; the 2,500円 purchase also remains below 3,000円, so shipping costs 200円. Translation of the question: “I have decided to buy a 2,500円 shirt as a present for a friend; I want it delivered by the day after tomorrow, and I also plan to add a message card. How much will it cost?” The relevant sentences are: 「送料は200円です。3,000円以上買うと、送料はかかりません。」, 「注文してから3日後に商品をお届けできます。」, 「注文した次の日にお届けするサービスをご利用される場合は、300円かかります。」 and 「メッセージカードをつける場合は、100円かかります。」 To avoid confusing it with (b), remember that (b) includes shipping and the card but forgets the 300円 expedited-delivery fee.
default.q.goukakumoshi2_n4-t12-q1.verdict:
✅ Correct answer: (c) 車の運転に気をつけていれば、歌っても大丈夫だと思っている。
The person thinks that singing is fine as long as they are careful while driving, because they always pay attention and have never caused an accident.
default.q.goukakumoshi2_n4-t12-q1.explanation: The pattern ～ていれば means “if/as long as someone does or is doing...,” while ～ても means “even if...”; 大丈夫だと思っています means “thinks that it is okay.” The supporting sentence is: 「でも、私は事故をおこさないように、気をつけているし、一度も事故をおこしたことはないので、大丈夫だと思っています。」, meaning “But I am careful not to cause an accident, and since I have never caused an accident, I think it is okay.” To distinguish this from (b) and (d), remember that 一度も事故をおこしたことはない means “has never caused an accident,” and the person does not decide to stop singing; they still believe singing is acceptable if they are careful.
default.q.goukakumoshi2_n4-t13-q1.verdict:
✅ Correct answer: (d) 電車とバスに乗るのが心配なこと
「そのこと」refers to the immediately preceding worry: Anna was very anxious because it was her first time using the train and bus and she might take the wrong one.
default.q.goukakumoshi2_n4-t13-q1.explanation: 「そのこと」is a demonstrative expression that refers to an event or idea mentioned immediately before. Here, it refers to the worry expressed as 「電車とバスを間違えたらどうしよう」, meaning “What should I do if I take the wrong train or bus?” The supporting sentence is: 「私は、電車とバスを使うのが初めてなので、「もし、電車とバスを間違えたらどうしよう」と、とても心配でした。」 Tip: 「電車とバスを間違えたこと」would mean that she actually took the wrong train or bus, but the passage only says that she was worried it might happen.
default.q.goukakumoshi2_n4-t13-q2.verdict:
✅ Correct answer: (c) 車でアンナさんを迎えに来てくれた。
Just before this, Yamada asked his father to drive to Anna’s apartment and pick her up. Therefore, when the father said 「もちろん、いいよ」, he agreed to do that.
default.q.goukakumoshi2_n4-t13-q2.explanation: The pattern 「～てくれる」 describes someone doing something beneficial for the speaker; 「迎えに来る」 means “come to pick someone up,” and 「車で」 indicates traveling by car. The question asks what the father did after agreeing, so the answer must match the action requested in the preceding sentence. The relevant original sentences are: 「山田さんはお父さんに、アパートまで車で迎えに来てくれるようにお願いしてくれました。」 and 「山田さんのお父さんは、すぐに『もちろん、いいよ』と言ってくれました。」 Option (d) is easy to confuse with the request, but Yamada made the request, while the father was the one who came by car to pick Anna up.
default.q.goukakumoshi2_n4-t13-q3.verdict:
✅ Correct answer: (a) 山田さんの家族は、だれもワインが飲めないから。
Yamada’s parents cannot drink alcohol, while Yamada and his younger sister are not allowed to drink it yet, so nobody in the family can drink the wine.
default.q.goukakumoshi2_n4-t13-q3.explanation: The pattern 「だれも～ない」 means “nobody” and states that no person can or does perform the action. The relevant sentence means: “Yamada’s father and mother cannot drink alcohol, and Yamada and his younger sister are not allowed to drink alcohol yet.” The supporting sentence is: 「しかし、山田さんのお父さんとお母さんはお酒が飲めないし、山田さんと妹さんは、まだお酒を飲んではいけません。」 To distinguish it from (d), 「飲めない」 means “cannot drink” or “are unable to drink,” while 「飲んではいけない」 means “must not drink” or “are not allowed to drink”; the passage uses the two expressions for different family members.
default.q.goukakumoshi2_n4-t13-q4.verdict:
✅ Correct answer: (d) 家族が好きなものを聞いておいたほうがよかった
Yamada’s family cannot drink the wine, so Anna regrets that she should have asked in advance what the family liked before buying a gift.
default.q.goukakumoshi2_n4-t13-q4.explanation: The pattern 「～ておいたほうがよかった」 means “should have done ～ beforehand” and expresses regret about something that should have been prepared in advance; 「聞いておく」 means to ask beforehand for preparation. The complete sentence 「おみやげを買うなら、家族が好きなものを聞いておいたほうがよかったと思いました。」 means “I thought that if I was going to buy a souvenir, I should have asked beforehand what the family liked.” The textual evidence is 「しかし、山田さんのお父さんとお母さんはお酒が飲めないし、山田さんと妹さんは、まだお酒を飲んではいけません。」 and 「おみやげを買うなら、家族が好きなものを聞いておいたほうがよかったと思いました。」. To distinguish it from (b), remember that the problem is not simply choosing wine instead of beer; Anna failed to ask about the whole family’s preferences and circumstances in advance.
default.q.goukakumoshi2_n4-t14-q1.verdict:
✅ Correct answer: (b) 受付であおぞら大学の利用カードを作る。
Lee is an exchange student at さくら大学, not a student at あおぞら大学, and this is Lee’s first time using the library. Therefore, Lee must make a library card at the reception desk first.
default.q.goukakumoshi2_n4-t14-q1.explanation: The pattern 「〜ではない大学の〜が、初めて図書館を利用するときは、受付で利用カードを作ってください」 means “when a student, international student, or teacher from a university other than あおぞら大学 uses the library for the first time, please make a library card at the reception desk”; 「〜ときは」 connects a situation or time, while 「〜てください」 expresses a request. Translation of the supporting sentence: “When students, international students, or teachers from a university other than あおぞら大学 use the library for the first time, they must make a library card at the reception desk.” The original sentence is: 「あおぞら大学ではない大学の大学生・留学生・先生が、初めて図書館を利用するときは、受付で利用カードを作ってください。」 To distinguish it from (a), remember that (a) says to use a card already issued by the university and applies only to people affiliated with あおぞら大学, whereas Lee belongs to さくら大学, so (b) is correct.
default.q.goukakumoshi2_n4-t14-q2.verdict:
✅ Correct answer: (a) 日曜日以外の日に受付に返す。
The library’s opening hours are listed only from Monday to Saturday, so a CD cannot be returned at the desk on Sunday. CDs must not be placed in the return box, so they must be returned at the desk on another day.
default.q.goukakumoshi2_n4-t14-q2.explanation: The key grammar is 「〜ないで」, meaning “without doing〜” or “do not do〜,” while 「必ず」 emphasizes “ 반드시, without fail,” so CDs and DVDs must be returned at the受付. The answer means, “A person returning a CD on Sunday should return it at the desk on a day other than Sunday.” The supporting sentence is: 「CD、DVDは返却ボックスに入れないで、必ず受付に返してください。」 and the listed opening hours cover only Monday through Saturday. To distinguish this from (c), remember that the return box may be used when the library is closed, but CDs and DVDs are an exception and must never be put in it.
default.q.goukakumoshi2_n4-t8-q1.verdict:
✅ Correct answer: (c) は
Here, は marks “the season I like best” as the topic, while 夏 gives information about that topic. Therefore, the pattern 「NはNです」 fits the sentence 「私が一番好きなきせつは夏です」.
default.q.goukakumoshi2_n4-t8-q1.explanation: The pattern 「NはNです」 uses は to introduce a topic and です to state or identify what that topic is; here, 「私が一番好きなきせつ」 is the topic and 夏 is the information stated about it. The sentence means: “The season I like best is summer.” The exact sentence in the passage is 「私が一番好きなきせつは夏です。」. To distinguish the closest options, remember that は is used for “A is B,” while に and と have different roles, and で would require a place, means, or cause meaning.
default.q.goukakumoshi2_n4-t8-q2.verdict:
✅ Correct answer: (b) ばかり
The sentence says that during the rainy season, it keeps raining continuously, so ばかり correctly follows 雨 and modifies ふっています.
default.q.goukakumoshi2_n4-t8-q2.explanation: The pattern 雨ばかりふっています means “it does nothing but rain” or “it keeps raining”; ばかり follows a noun to emphasize repetition or predominance. The sentence means: “June is called ‘the rainy season,’ and it keeps raining continuously.” The original sentence is: 「6月は「梅雨」と言ってずっと雨ばかりふっています。」A useful distinction is that しか also means “only,” but it must be paired with a negative form, whereas ばかり can be used with an affirmative verb such as ふっています.
default.q.goukakumoshi2_n4-t8-q3.verdict:
✅ Correct answer: (a) 行かなくてもいいです
Because summer vacation begins, the children do not have to go to school.
default.q.goukakumoshi2_n4-t8-q3.explanation: The pattern 行かなくてもいいです is formed with the negative verb form + てもいいです and means “do not have to do” or “it is okay not to do.” Here, 夏休みがはじまるので shows that summer vacation begins, so the children do not need to go to school. The sentence means: “Because summer vacation begins, the children do not have to go to school.” The original sentence is: 「7月になると、夏休みがはじまるので、子どもたちは学校に行かなくてもいいです。」A useful distinction is that 行かなくてはなりません means “must go,” which is the opposite of 行かなくてもいいです.
default.q.goukakumoshi2_n4-t8-q4.verdict:
✅ Correct answer: (d) 遊んだり
The pattern 「Vたり、Vたりします」 lists representative activities; here, 「遊んだり」 is parallel with 「行ったり」 and 「したり」.
default.q.goukakumoshi2_n4-t8-q4.explanation: The pattern 「Vたり、Vたりします」 means “do things such as V1 and V2” and lists representative actions; each verb takes 「たり」, with the sentence ending in 「します」. The sentence means: “The children play with their friends, go to the pool, do their homework, and so on.” The original sentence is: 「子どもたちは友だちと遊んだり、プールへ行ったり、宿題をしたりします。」 A useful distinction is that 「遊んだり」 lists an activity, while 「遊んだら」 means “if/after playing,” so it cannot match the sequence 「行ったり、したり」.
default.q.goukakumoshi2_n4-t8-q5.verdict:
✅ Correct answer: (a) だけど
The conjunction 「だけど」 expresses contrast, connecting the heat of summer in Japan with the author's continued enjoyment of the season.
default.q.goukakumoshi2_n4-t8-q5.explanation: The conjunction 「だけど」, an informal spoken form of 「けれども」 or 「でも」, stands at the beginning of an independent sentence and expresses contrast, meaning "but" or "however." The context describes Japan’s summer as extremely hot: 「8月は一番暑い月です。... 日本の夏は暑いですが、海やプール、花火大会、おまつりなど、おもしろいことがたくさんあります。」 The completed sentence 「だけど私は夏が大好きです。」 means: "However, I really love summer," clearly contrasting the speaker’s feelings with the previously mentioned heat. Do not confuse it with 「だから」 or 「それに」, which express cause or addition, or with 「もし」, which requires a conditional predicate rather than a directly affirmative statement.
default.q.goukakumoshi2_n4-t8-q5.why.0: ✓ (a) 「だけど」(but/however) is the most suitable conjunction for expressing that the author still likes summer even though the weather is extremely hot.
default.q.goukakumoshi2_n4-t8-q5.why.1: ✗ (b) 「だから」 (“therefore/so”) is a conjunction indicating a result following a cause-and-effect relationship. It is not used in a contrasting context.
default.q.goukakumoshi2_n4-t8-q5.why.2: ✗ (c) 「それに」(moreover, in addition) is a conjunction that adds information in the same direction, so it is unsuitable for connecting sentences expressing a contrastive change.
default.q.goukakumoshi2_n4-t8-q5.why.3: ✗ (d) 「もし」 (“if”/“supposing”) is an adverb used together with conditional patterns such as ～たら or ～ば; it cannot stand alone as a conjunction introducing an affirmative sentence.
default.q.goukakumoshi2_n4-t9-q1.verdict:
✅ Correct answer: (c) 宿題をする。
The mother tells 美花さん to finish her homework before eating the grapes. Therefore, doing homework is the first thing she must do.
default.q.goukakumoshi2_n4-t9-q1.explanation: The pattern ～たら means “when/after doing…”, and it marks the condition or time for the following action. 宿題が終わったら食べてください。 means “After you finish your homework, eat the grapes.” The supporting sentence in the passage is: 「冷蔵庫の中に、ぶどうが入っているので、宿題が終わったら食べてください。」 Tip: ぶどうを食べる happens after 宿題をする, while おばあちゃんに電話をかける happens あとで, meaning “later.”

「上着」 is read 「うわぎ」 (jacket, outer garment).

The other three options are real readings or look-alike words that do not fit this word, so read every option to the end before choosing. Full sentence: もっと （つよく） おしてください。

default.q.goukakumoshi2_n4-t7-q3.explanation: This sentence combines the prohibition pattern 「Vてはいけない」(must not do something) with the nominalizing pattern 「plain form + ということ」, which turns a clause into a noun phrase meaning "the fact/matter that..." and makes it the object of the cognition verb 「知っています」. The complete meaning is: "You know that you must not smoke here, right?" For comparison: 明日テストがあるということを忘れないでください (Please do not forget that there is a test tomorrow.) In sentence-order questions, first combine familiar grammar chunks such as 「吸ってはいけない」, then look at the final verb: 「知っています」requires an object marked by を, so 「ということを」must come directly before it.

The particle 「まで」 follows the location noun 「部屋」 and limits the destination to that nearby place. The full meaning of the dialogue is: A asks, “Has Mr. Tanaka come back yet?” and B replies, “I’m going to the room to take a quick look, and I’ll be right back.” A useful strategy for this type of question is to combine the fixed phrases from the end backward, first forming 「見に行ってきます」 and then placing the location phrase 「部屋まで」 at the beginning. A similar example is: 「ちょっとコンビニまで飲み物を買いに行ってきます。」 (I’m going to the convenience store to buy some drinks and will be back shortly).

default.q.goukakumoshi2_n4-t7-q5.explanation: This question tests the formation of a noun-modifying clause combined with the potential pattern 「V-る + ことができる」(can do V). Here, the adverb 「たくさん」(a lot) comes before the dictionary-form verb 「話す」, creating 「日本語をたくさん話すことができる」, which directly modifies the noun 「クラス」. The complete sentence is 「日本語をたくさん話すことができるクラスはありますか。」(Are there any classes where learners can speak a lot of Japanese?) The key is to identify the main noun before the final particle 「は」, then place the dictionary-form verb + ことができる before it as a modifier. For additional practice, compare: 「静かに本を読むことができる場所を探しています。」(I am looking for a place where I can read quietly.)
